Thanks for the ping, Karthik — good ask and reasonable compliance/audit use case. A few quick thoughts and options (short vs medium term):

Short term (2–4 weeks):
- Provide a one-off enriched billing export for Acme: we can join request logs to billing documents by timestamp+customer-id and produce a route-level CSV they can reconcile offline. Low engineering cost, manual prep.
- Add per-route percentile summary (p50/p95) to existing Console Usage -> Performance tab as a temporary table. No deep storage changes, just an aggregation job against recent metrics.

Medium term (2–3 months):
- Add route_id tagging into our billing pipeline so exports include a route column by default. This requires adding route metadata to the billing ingestion records and increasing retention of request-level references for 90 days.
- Build a per-route dashboard in the Console with cost-attribution, latency percentiles, and link-to-trace drilldowns (click to view the associated sampled trace or request-id).

Risks / tradeoffs:
- Storage and cost: retaining request-level references for 90 days will increase storage and invoiced costs; we should estimate expected growth for top-20 accounts.
- PII/privacy: ensure route metadata doesn't leak customer PII; route names should be sanitized.
- SLAs: adding request->invoice linking is best-effort; exact matching may fail for async/batched billing entries.

Ask to Eng (Evelyn): can you do a quick feasibility + storage delta estimate for the medium-term path? If we can do a one-off export quickly, we can buy time. Thanks.

- Ava
Ava Chen
Product Manager, Console | Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Ava — quick feasibility note from Eng. High level: medium-term path is doable but non-trivial. Implementation outline and blockers:

1) Instrumentation: we need to ensure each incoming request carries a stable route_id and customer_id that persists through batching. This is largely in place for most routes but there are edge cases (batching, job-mode ingestion) that will need work.
2) Billing pipeline change: augment billing record schema with optional route_id field; adjust aggregation and CSV exporter. Expected schema change is small but touches downstream systems (billing reconciliation).
3) Storage/retention: to support link-to-trace we need to keep sampled request references for 60–90 days. Rough estimate: for top-100 customers this is ~1.2TB additional indexed storage/month (back-of-envelope). Need finance signoff for cost to customers or internal absorption.
4) Trace linking: we'll return a request-id that can be looked up in our trace store. For privacy/compliance we can add a gated role that allows viewing these links.

Estimate: 6–8 engineer-weeks to implement medium-term (one backend engineer + one infra SRE + frontend PM/engineer for Console dashboard). Short-term one-off export + simple per-route percentile table: ~5 engineer-days to produce an initial export and a temporary dashboard.

Open questions:
- Do we offer the medium-term feature as an account-level opt-in (preferred) or enable globally?
- Who owns the customer communications about potential extra charges for increased retention? (Finance?)

I can scope a more detailed RFC if product wants to proceed.

—Evelyn
